history.value: Thrive Capital was founded in New York in 2009 by Joshua Kushner, then 24, with a $5M first fund. It backed Instagram, Warby Parker and GitHub early, co-founded Oscar Health, led rounds in Stripe, Slack and Affirm, and since 2023 has been OpenAI's largest venture shareholder. Its tenth fund closed at over $10B in February 2026.
history.basis: founding and early book per Wikipedia and Fortune 2014-10-06; Oscar per the IPO Form 3 and the Claremount TW vehicle (decisions.md 1/5); Stripe/Slack/Affirm/Instagram/GitHub rounds per the citations in base.csv; OpenAI/SpaceX/Databricks/Anduril/Cursor per TechCrunch 2026-02-17 and the Aug-2026 investor letter (Bloomberg 2026-08-14); Fund X per the firm's own /thrive-x page; RAUM per the 2026-07-06 ADV; Holdings and Eternal per decisions.md 2-3. Rewritten to the reader-facing shape (PRO-147, 2026-09-24). Outside the venture firm and not counted in the portfolio: Thrive Holdings (the AI buy-and-build holding company, spun out 2025) and Thrive Eternal (permanent capital for sports and cultural assets, 2026), decisions.md 2-3. Fund X's split ($1B early stage, $9B growth), the $50.5B managed and the SpaceX, Databricks, Anduril and Cursor positions are in the basis above.

investment_stage.basis: DERIVED, no site filters exist: the fund architecture separates an early-stage sleeve from a growth sleeve (Thrive X: $1B early / $9B growth; every flagship since VI carries a Growth L.P.) and the Opportunity funds back late rounds and secondaries; the landed base reads Seed 47 / Series A 44 / Growth 79 of 170 entries (Growth = Series B+ incl. secondaries and tenders), Pre-Seed absent. Late Stage from the Opportunity vehicles and the secondary-built positions (OpenAI, SpaceX, Spotify)

investment_geo.basis: DERIVED, no site filters exist: hq_country on the 170-row base is US 157 / BR 3 / GB 2 / DE 2 / None 2 / SE 2 / DK 1 / CA 1; the firm's one office is New York (ADV Item 1.F) and 71 of 170 HQs are New York — a US core with European and Latin American positions, none marketed as a territory

investment_scope.basis: DERIVED from the grind's focus column (169 of 170 rows classified into data/taxonomy/focus.json after the post-close delta): Consumer & Marketplaces 42, Healthcare & Bio 28, Fintech & Payments 28, SaaS 18, Media, Gaming & Advertising 11, Industrial & Robotics 9, AI & Applied AI 9, Security 6, Climate & Energy 5, Crypto & Web3 5, Data Infrastructure 4, DevTools & APIs 4 — published above 7 companies (~4% of the base; config profile.focus_min_companies). Generalist: no single-sector thesis. The firm's own vocabulary is one sentence ('internet, software, and technology-enabled companies'); the AI-era book (OpenAI, Anysphere, Physical Intelligence, Sierra, OpenEvidence, Chai, Databricks, Essential AI, io) classifies by what each company sells, so AI reads low here relative to the firm's positioning

investment_range.basis: Median: partner-anchored entry-round median $19,982,390 across 34 membership-verified base companies with priced Form D histories (scratch/verified-median.json; p25 $8.5M, p75 $40.5M), published as $20M — thin (34 of 155 members: no site or fund-filing layer anchors most rows) and a round-size proxy for check size, fair only where Thrive led. | Lower limit: the documented smallest-entry class — Grailed's $1.6M seed filing (2015) and Warby Parker's $1.5M seed round (2011), both Thrive participations; no program floor exists (no accelerator). | Upper limit: the ~$1.3B commitment to OpenAI in the Oct-2024 $6.6B round (Thrive led; press-reported share) — the largest verified single check; the $10B Databricks Series J and the $2.1B Isomorphic Series B were Thrive-led rounds whose Thrive share is undisclosed. Dry-powder check: Fund X's $9B growth sleeve supports $0.9-1.35B positions at 10-15% concentration

notable_investments.basis: Recognition over the confirmed base only: all eight are ledger members (OpenAI, Stripe, Databricks, Anysphere and Oscar Health via the firm's own job board plus press/filings; Instagram, GitHub and Spotify as cited recall rows) — asserted by build-firm-profile.py against ledger verdicts on the 170-row base

funds.basis: 17 entries, Funds I-X with their growth sleeves, the Supplemental and the first Opportunity fund. Direct raises carry filed sold amounts asserted against the filings at build time (13 entries with accessions); Fund III carries its press close ($150M) with the $147M filing as corroboration; Fund X's two L.P.s filed 'Indefinite' at $0 sold (Oct 2025) so their sizes are the firm's own /thrive-x statement; Fund I predates Form D electronic filing. Treatment of the rest: the lettered co-invest/SPV LLCs and L.P.s (III-A, IV-C/D, IV Stripe, VI-A…L, VII-B, VIII-B/C/D, VIII Growth-A/B/D, IX-A/C, IX Growth-B…G, X-A, X Growth-A/B, 'Harry's') and the Claremount entities are deal and GP-side vehicles (decisions.md ruling 1), not funds — 24 such vehicles file Form Ds totalling ~$2.9B sold, and JSC Capital Partners ($326M sold, 2024) and North River Angel Investments IX ($10M, 2025) are ADV-listed umbrella funds outside the flagship families; all are listed in sources/edgar/fund-formds.json and the ADV roster, none in this table
